nodes.recap: chapter header + alone in the hall
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 20          |
-------------------------------


$CThe hall is elliptical, and enormous, and quiet.##

You did not come through the doors.# You do not know
how you came to be here, only that you are here
and that the others are not.# You registered their absence
without alarm as the moment resolved around you,
as if it were the right thing, the expected thing.#
This hall is for two.##

The floor is white marble so polished it is almost a mirror:#
you can see the faint shape of yourself reflected in it,
standing alone at the northern end while the hall
extends away from you toward a wide staircase
at the southern end, flanked by four great entrances,
each one hung with enormous translucent drapes
that move gently in air that has no detectable source.##

The light is oblique, banded, gold and white
coming through tall windows, and the ceiling is very high and frescoed
and you are not going to think about the ceiling right now,
because the drapes on the left-hand entrance
have just stopped moving.##

Everything stops.# The drapes, the light, the air itself.##

And then she steps through.##

The armor is old, older than anything you have seen on this planet,
and that is not a small claim.# Full plate, greaves and gauntlets
and breastplate and gorget, and a great helm that covers everything
above the shoulders in a curve of dark greenish metal engraved
with lines you cannot read.##

She carries two swords: long, slightly curved sabers,
gold handles, blades the color of blue glass,
an impossible material that is neither steel nor crystal
but something that has the properties of both.#
They hang at her sides, points downward, held in a grip
that is more frightening than any guard.##

She is tall inside the armor and she moves the way nothing
in that weight of metal should be able to move,
balanced and fluid, like someone who has worn this particular suit
long enough that it has become a second skin.##

She crosses to the hall's other focus, the far point of the ellipse,
and she looks at you through the slits of her helm.##

A thousand voices ring in your head at once,
and you almost believe you see the air between you vibrate
with the flow of that energy:#

$G<<I am Saberinne.>>$C##

Before you can register a single syllable of that,
she comes at you.##

nodes.recap: the duel with Saberinne - Kriss is losing, fights with desperate rage
nodes.text:
Blind instinct draws your sword from its scabbard.##

Your mind is not concerned, in that moment, with being a student
from Earth who has never properly trained with a weapon.#
There is only your movement and hers, her sabers
cutting the air, silent and precise, and the sword
in both your hands that has been part of you
for so many months it answers before you think.##

You clash.# The impact sends sparks in a cascade across the mirror floor
that leave no trace on the marble.# You slide,
get your footing back, and come at her again.##

You are fighting with the force of desperation,
the determination not to yield,
and nothing else.# She reads every initiative
as if she can see inside your mind.#
Every counter you attempt she is already past.#
And for every meter you take, you give back two.##

The wall is approaching behind you.##

encounter.victorymessage:
$CYou are against the wall.##

Right hand gripping your sword, left hand pressed flat
to the cold marble behind you.# Her saber is at your throat.#
The helm's slits look at you, steady, unhurried.##

You have fought as you have never imagined any person could fight,
and you have lost.# The thought does not arrive with resignation.
It arrives with something else entirely:
that same pressure behind your hands,
behind your eyes, the same rage that tore a metal door
out of its frame in the dark of an underwater cell.##

You cannot let it end like this.# You will not.##

You think of all of them, of every day of this journey,
and you close your fist around your sword and pour everything
you have into it: your rage, your desperation,
every charged particle of the power that has been
building in you since Noi-Hert took you in.#
And you scream.# A full-throated scream
you have never heard yourself make before.##

The sword tears free of the wall's gravity and flashes upward,
striking her helm with a force so tremendous
that for one instant both your eyes are blinded
by the screech of wounded metal.##

The helm spins away down the staircase behind her.# The light returns.##
encounter.defeatmessage:
$CShe has ten thousand years of practice,
and every second of it.##

The marble is cold under your back.#
The hall's ceiling is very beautiful,
and you have a great deal of time to look at it.##

nodes.text:
Time resumes.##

The armor seems to breathe, then to recede, drawing back
into itself until it is gone, and what it reveals
is a woman who has no equivalent in anything
you have seen before or will see again.##

She is beautiful in a way that has no relation to age,
because age has not touched her.# Not young, not old,
but $Woutside of time$C entirely, as if time long ago decided
it could not find the purchase on her that it finds
on everyone else and moved on without her.#
Her face is the face of something ancient that has remained
completely itself.##

Blonde curls fall around her face and down her back,
spilling over the white dress that reveals a perfect figure.#
Her eyes are the color of the sea at a depth where the sun
still reaches, green and clear and containing
a great warmth and an even greater strength.##

She looks at you with those eyes and she smiles.
$C##

$G"I am Saberinne"$C she says,
and projects that warmth directly into your mind.##

You know her voice.##

$c<<I know it.# I have been hearing it since Ayonn,
in dreams, at the edge of sleep,
between one breath and the next in the dark.#
I know this voice.# I found her.>>$C##

nodes.recap: companions recover - Saberinne leads everyone to the terrace - revelations begin

dialogues.precomment:
Your companions, you discover, were behind you the whole time
and noticed nothing of the duel.# They are still recovering
from the general stupor of the arrival, looking around
the hall in varying states of wonder.##

Efeliah recovers first.# She looks at Saberinne
and does something you have never seen her do:
she goes to her knees, bowing her head.# Smiurl drops
beside her without hesitation, his skin flooding a reverent blue-violet.#
Theo and Corolla stay on their feet, staring.##

Saberinne looks at Efeliah with a warmth that is also a correction.
dialogues.line:
Rise.# I am not what you think.#
I am a human being, the same as you.
dialogues.comment: She says it without vanity and without false modesty.##

dialogues.line:
Come. Follow me out to the terrace.#
I believe I owe you a great many explanations.
dialogues.comment:
She turns toward the northern entrance,
and they follow her down a corridor of equal splendor,
frescoed ceilings, marble walls, tall bright windows
that pour oblique light across the floor.##

You and Saberinne walk ahead of the others, and you look
at each other, and she looks back at you,
and whatever passes between your minds in that moment
is entirely beyond even Efeliah's perception.##

dialogues.precomment:
The corridor opens onto a wide covered terrace, pergola-style,
framed by climbing plants that must be tended with enormous care,
the whole structure inclining just slightly toward the liberty style.
A small table is already set.# Servants bring refreshments.
They are two young people who smile easily and bow at Saberinne.
dialogues.line:
I do not permit slavery in this city.#
Service in the palace is considered a privilege,
and given freely.
dialogues.comment:
She says it briefly, because it is simply how things are.##

They sit.# Saberinne watches them eat with the expression
of someone reading a very interesting page,
and then her attention settles on Kriss,
chinning her hand, something warm and intent in her face.##

dialogues.precomment: When they have eaten, she begins.
dialogues.line:
Kriss, I perceived your presence from the day
you arrived on Noi-Hert, born from the deepest fiber
of our universe.# I knew of your coming.# It was prophesied.
And even had it not been, all of this would have happened anyway.

You come from a parallel universe.#
You did not travel through your own space or time.
What made the crossing possible was two things:
the lightning that struck near you, in an unusual storm
that altered the energetic parameters of your surroundings,
and, more importantly, your own mind.##

As you can all see, my mind is well outside the common.#
No one else on this planet could have perceived Kriss's arrival
from such a distance. And no one else could have sustained
a city like this in a world in full decay.
dialogues.comment: She pauses and looks at Kriss.##

dialogues.line:
When the lightning caught you, your mind placed
our two universes in contact, unconsciously.#
Because this universe, as you were told at Seer's Rock,
has additional dimensions: they enable the exchange
between minds, and they permit the rarest minds
to alter the reality of ordinary physical law.##

Yours is one of those minds.
dialogues.comment:
Efeliah makes a small, involuntary sound.#

$g<<The structures.# The ones I always perceived
but could not name.>>$C##

dialogues.line:
Exactly.# You would call it, somewhat imprecisely, telekinesis.
Those neural circuits were unused in your life before this,
because they were genuinely useless in your universe.
When you arrived here, the energy of your mind
began pressing on them automatically.##

The night you saved Smiurl from the Sgozza-Buoi,
Efeliah's emotional transmission overloaded
your mental equilibrium. It was like flooring a cold engine:
your mind ran hot and nearly damaged itself.#
But that event was crucial. From that evening,
the pathway was unlocked.##

Then the door in the underwater cell.#
And from that moment, hour by hour, day by day,
your potential grew enormously.#
I could move a mountain now, if I wanted to.
Do you believe me?

dialogues.comment: A pause for all of them to absorb this.##

dialogues.line:
Wait.# The legend.# The one Elder Long told us,
about the Master dreaming of a golden goddess
who told him to expect us.

dialogues.precomment: She tilts her head, genuinely surprised.
dialogues.line:
That I did not know.# I transmitted to him what knowledge
I could in the few years our meeting allowed.#
Your community is the product of that encounter.#
But a dream predicting your arrival?#
That is something he built himself, it seems.#
The circumstances make it remarkable, I grant you.

dialogues.precomment:
Saberinne looks at the city through the terrace arch,
at the walls, at the siege camp beyond them,
and the warmth in her face becomes something else:
some ancient weight that lives below everything.##
dialogues.line:
This city is my life.# It bears my name,
and since it has lived, I have lived.#
If it were destroyed, it would mean destruction for my soul as well.##

It has no army.# It is part of our constitution.#
Our isolation and our walls have always been sufficient.
Until now.# Dozens of Hordes have formed an alliance
to take its resources, the only technological wealth left intact
anywhere on this planet.##

I cannot defend it alone.# But there may be another way.

nodes.recap: Saberinne explains the mind-merge; then private time in the garden

dialogues.precomment:
She leads them down the terrace stairs into the gardens:
fountains, flowers, trees bending in the warm breeze.
She walks barefoot on the grass.##
dialogues.line:
Two minds joined at their fullest depth.
Not communication.# More than that.#
Not memory-sharing.# More than that.##

If our minds can truly fuse into a single entity,
its power would multiply beyond anything either of us
could achieve alone.# It could reach every mind
in that army simultaneously and simply... stop them.##

But I first need to understand something
I have been considering since the moment you arrived here.
Kriss, I would like to speak with you privately.
dialogues.comment:
She says it without apology, because she does not need any.##

$c<<I would not refuse for anything in the world.>>$C##

dialogues.precomment:
The others exchange glances.# Corolla opens her mouth,
then closes it, something in Saberinne's expression
not quite an instruction but carrying the weight of one.##
dialogues.comment:
She says it flatly.# Efeliah respectfully withdraws
even her mental presence.##

dialogues.precomment:
Saberinne leads you through the gardens to a hedge maze,
along passages of perfect green, until the passages open
into a small clearing at the center: a stone bench,
a fountain playing quietly, flowers growing close to the water.##

You sit.# Your mind and heart feel as if they will crack open.
So many thoughts, so many emotions pressing at once
that no word can form.##

She raises one finger to her lips, smiling.
dialogues.comment:
She says it softly, into your mind.##

And so you don't.##

You sit facing each other, and your eyes find hers,
and what happens then is not conversation, not in any form
you have a name for.# You are looking directly
into each other's minds, past every surface,
and what is there is... exact.# Perfectly complementary.
Two things that were built to find each other.##

No words. No images.# The language is emotion itself.#
Every neuron you have vibrating in time with every thought she has.
You can feel her breathing on your face,
counting the molecules of air between you in time
that stretches like honey.# Her hands find yours,
meeting in the middle.##

You could stay here for an eternity.# You both know this.
The want is very strong.##

A single bird, alone in the sky above the hedge, sings.##

nodes.recap: return to the others - soulmate reveal - Corolla's reaction
nodes.text:
You walk back to the others in the late afternoon,
your arm through hers.##

Saberinne takes her leave with the composure she carries
in everything, though she holds your gaze a half-second longer
than she holds anyone else's, a farewell
that only you can read.##

The moment she is gone, Corolla says, loudly,
without the smallest concern about being overheard:#

$R"What in the world did she say to you for all that time?!"$C##

$c<<Nothing.# We did not exchange a single word.>>$C##

$CAn uncomfortable silence.# Then Efeliah comes forward,
her face carrying something between concern and wonder.##

$g"Kriss... Something has changed in you.# Profoundly.
I almost don't recognize you..."$C##

$Y"Are you alright?"$C Smiurl asks, looking from Ef to you,
already anxious at the others' expressions.##

$B"I believe so,"$C says Theo, without turning from the window
where he has been watching the garden.# The others look at him,
not understanding.# Finally you speak.##

$c"Do you know the concept of kindred souls?"$C##

Efeliah explains it to the others.##

$c"I stopped believing in things like that as a child.#
The facts have now shown me I was wrong.##

"My mind and Saberinne's are perfectly complementary.
They can merge into a single entity without resistance..."$C##

$g"In the garden, you were exchanging thoughts.#
Looking into each other's minds."$C Ef says.##

$c"Yes."$C##

$R"Are you certain?"$C asks Corolla, sharp.##

$c"Yes."$C##

$g"He's not telling us everything,"$C Ef thinks, then catches herself,
then looks up to find you watching her.##

$g"How did you..."$C##

$c"I heard you.# Only Saberinne has ever been able
to see past your screens before, hasn't she?"$C##

Efeliah stares at you, stunned.##

$c"We are one thing now.# Two faces of the same coin.
My life is hers, her city is mine,
and our hearts have become a single heartbeat..."$C##

Corolla drops onto the edge of the nearest bed
and stares at the ceiling.##

$R"What has happened to you..."$C she murmurs,
half to herself.##

$c"Nothing bad.# I promise you that."$C
You put a hand on her shoulder.#
$c"You are still my best friends.
The finest companions anyone has ever had.##

"But my life is now bound to Saberinne's.
In every place, in every time."$C##

nodes.recap: night falls - Saberinne brings them to their quarters
nodes.text:
With that, you each retire to your rooms.##

Saberinne has arranged everything: palatial quarters,
warm water, clean clothes, a quiet that is not
the quiet of a besieged city but the quiet of one
that has decided, at some depth, that it will survive the morning.##

You wash, change, and for a long time stand at the window
looking out over the gardens in the last of the light,
over the walls, over the camp fires of the army
that has no idea what is waiting for it.##

$c<<Tomorrow.>>$C##

You turn from the window and go to meet the others for dinner.##
